notes: Profiles are deterministic wrappers, not free-form scanner commands.
Every profile must validate scope before planning or execution.
External tools must be installed by scripts/redscope-tool-installer.ts first.

profiles.name: Passive Company Recon
profiles.description: Prepare a passive reconnaissance evidence workspace for an authorized organization or domain without target probing.
stopConditions: Stop if the requested organization or domain is not listed in scope.
Do not directly probe scoped targets.
Do not enumerate subdomains with active DNS brute force.
Only collect or prepare passive evidence sources.

steps.description: Record scoped organization and domain seeds.
Create a passive source checklist for analyst review.

profiles.name: Baseline URL Review
profiles.description: Perform a low-impact single-URL baseline review for an explicitly scoped URL.
stopConditions: Stop if the target URL is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Stop after one HTTP request unless redirected to the same host.
Do not crawl, fuzz, brute force, authenticate, or submit forms.

steps.description: Fetch the authorized URL once and record status, final URL, and response headers.

profiles.name: Repository Secret and SAST Review
profiles.description: Run authorized local repository review with pinned project-local tools.
stopConditions: Stop if the repository path is not listed in scope.
Do not upload source code or findings to third-party services.
Run local read-only scans only.

steps.description: Run gitleaks detect with redacted output.
Run semgrep in local-only JSON mode.

profiles.name: Authorized Gitleaks Secret Scan
profiles.description: Run a separately approved local Gitleaks secret scan for an explicitly scoped repository with per-tool scanner allowlisting.
stopConditions: Stop if restricted testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the repository path is not listed in scope.targets.repositories.
Run only when gitleaks is listed in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.
Run local read-only secret detection only.
Use redacted JSON output and do not upload source code or findings to third-party services.
Keep raw secret values out of reports, memory, and delivery artifacts.

steps.description: Run gitleaks detect with redacted local JSON output when approved in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.

profiles.name: Authorized Semgrep SAST
profiles.description: Run a separately approved local Semgrep SAST scan for an explicitly scoped repository with a project-local Semgrep config and per-tool scanner allowlisting.
stopConditions: Stop if restricted testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the repository path is not listed in scope.targets.repositories.
Run only when semgrep is listed in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.
Use only a project-local Semgrep config or an explicitly supplied --semgrep-config path.
Run local read-only static analysis only.
Do not upload source code, findings, metrics, or rule telemetry to third-party services.

steps.description: Run semgrep in local-only JSON mode when approved in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.

profiles.name: Threat Trace Artifact Review
profiles.description: Summarize authorized local logs, SIEM exports, STIX bundles, EVTX metadata, archives, IOCs, and incident artifacts without copying raw contents into reports.
stopConditions: Stop if the artifact path is not listed in scope.
Do not upload logs, IOCs, or artifacts to third-party services.
Do not copy raw log lines, payloads, secrets, or full artifact contents into reports.
Only generate local metadata, hashes, capped indicator samples, structured parser summaries, and defensive triage guidance.

steps.description: Index local artifact metadata, hashes, indicator counts, timestamp bounds, threat-trace keyword counts, and structured parser summaries.
Record defensive triage questions and next-step containment guidance for analyst review.

profiles.name: Authorized HTTP Probe
profiles.description: Run a bounded httpx probe against explicitly scoped URLs or domains.
stopConditions: Stop if any target is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Do not crawl, fuzz, brute force, authenticate, or submit forms.
Respect the lower of profile and scope rate limits.

steps.description: Run httpx with JSON output, bounded concurrency, and low rate.

profiles.name: Authorized Nuclei Low-Impact Scan
profiles.description: Run a low-impact nuclei profile for explicitly authorized targets and templates.
stopConditions: Stop if active testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if any target is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Use low/info severity templates only.
Do not run exploit, fuzzing, brute-force, credential, file-upload, or destructive templates.

steps.description: Run nuclei with low/info severity, JSONL output, and strict rate limits.

profiles.name: Authorized Third-Party Scanner Baseline
profiles.description: Run separately approved low-impact third-party scanner steps against explicitly scoped targets with written scanner approval and per-tool allowlisting.
stopConditions: Stop if restricted testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if any target is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Run only tools listed in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.
Use httpx only for low-rate HTTP metadata probing.
Use nuclei only with low/info severity templates.
Do not run exploit, fuzzing, brute-force, credential, file-upload, destructive, or state-changing scanner checks.
Do not crawl beyond the supplied target list or submit forms.
Respect the lower of profile and scope rate limits.
Keep scanner outputs local and normalize findings before delivery.

steps.description: Run httpx with JSON output, bounded concurrency, and low rate when approved in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.
Run nuclei with low/info severity, JSONL output, and strict rate limits when approved in scope.scannerExecution.allowedTools.

profiles.name: Authorized Low-Impact Validator
profiles.description: Run separately approved same-origin GET/HEAD validators that can promote only proven scoped impact to target-verified issues without executing public PoC code.
stopConditions: Stop if active testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the target URL is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Run only validators declared in scope.validation.validators with separate approval metadata.
Each validator may make at most one same-origin GET or HEAD request with no request body.
Do not execute arbitrary PoC code, exploit payloads, fuzzing, brute-force, credential, upload, or destructive checks.
Do not follow cross-origin redirects or validate paths outside the scoped target URL.
Store response metadata, header digests, body sample hashes, and assertion outcomes only; do not store raw response body text.
Promote to target-verified-issue only when the approved low-impact assertion passes against the scoped target.

steps.description: Execute scope-declared low-impact GET/HEAD validators and write target-verified evidence only for passing assertions.

profiles.name: Authorized Business Logic Validation
profiles.description: Validate separately approved business-logic test cases for authorization, IDOR, payment/refund/coupon, workflow-state, upload, and SQL injection evidence while keeping intrusive actions evidence-only by default.
stopConditions: Stop if active testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the target URL is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Run only business-logic test cases declared in scope.logicValidation.testCases with separate approval metadata.

safe-readonly-http cases may use only same-origin GET or HEAD requests, no request body, manual redirects, and declared actor sessions supplied from environment variables or same-origin login bootstrap.
Do not store raw response bodies, cookies, bearer tokens, or actor session header values.
Do not execute arbitrary PoC code, fuzzing, brute-force, credential stuffing, payment capture, destructive upload, or raw SQL injection payloads by default.
Payment, refund, coupon, workflow-state, upload, and SQL injection checks must remain evidence-only unless a future profile adds a separately reviewed runner.
Parallel lanes are planning metadata only; analyst/subagent execution must keep stateful tests serial and confirm no shared target state.
Promote to target-verified-issue only when safe read-only actor checks prove impact or approved evidence-only records include observedImpact=true and evidence references.

steps.description: Evaluate scope-declared business-logic test cases, produce parallel review lanes, and write target-verified findings only for proven target impact.

profiles.name: Authorized Stateful Business Logic Validation
profiles.description: Run separately reviewed same-origin state-changing business-logic HTTP test cases for payment/refund/coupon/workflow-state, upload, SQL-injection evidence, and related workflows only when the scope explicitly approves the change window and rollback plan.
stopConditions: Stop if active testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the target URL is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Run only test cases with validationMode approved-state-changing-http.
Each executed test case may send one fixed same-origin POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE request with a reviewed scope body or requestBodyEnv value.
Honor logicValidation.stateChangingApproval.maxMutatingRequests, defaulting to one mutating request per run.
Do not execute arbitrary PoC code, generated fuzz payloads, brute force, credential stuffing, payment capture, destructive upload, or scanner templates.
Do not store raw request bodies, raw response bodies, cookies, bearer tokens, or actor session header values.
Require an approved change window and rollback plan before any mutating request.
Promote to target-verified-issue only when the mutating request succeeds, observedImpact=true, and approved evidence references are present.

steps.description: Execute scope-declared fixed state-changing HTTP business-logic test cases and write target-verified findings only after observed target impact is evidenced.

profiles.name: Authorized PoC Candidate Validation
profiles.description: Fingerprint an explicitly scoped target with header/body/cookie signatures, map product/vendor/CPE hints, merge owner-confirmed version evidence, score historical vulnerability evidence against local and external PoC/template sources plus authoritative advisory metadata, and produce non-exploit validation gates with screenshot evidence slots.
stopConditions: Stop if active testing is not explicitly present in scope.testLevels.
Stop if the target is not in scope or is explicitly excluded.
Do not execute arbitrary PoC code from tools/sources.
Only match fingerprints, same-context versions, and historical vulnerability identifiers to candidate PoC/template files.
Use scope.technologyEvidence when available to separate owner-confirmed target versions from public-intelligence leads.
Treat reviewed template status as an allowlist decision, not as blanket trust for an entire repository.
External PoC search may query GitHub and public search engines with fingerprint terms only; do not include target hostnames in search queries.
External search results are metadata links only; do not download or execute PoC code from search results.
Vulnerability advisory enrichment may query NVD with CPE/CVE/product/version fingerprint terms only; do not treat public advisory metadata as proof of exploitability.
Automatic validation gates check evidence correlation only; do not run exploit payloads or arbitrary PoC code.
Keep public-intelligence leads, target fingerprint correlations, owner-confirmed target versions, and target-verified issues as separate evidence classes.
Keep weak product-only hits as triage-only leads instead of validation attempts.
Any follow-up validation must use a separately reviewed low-impact profile or manual analyst approval.
Screenshots must avoid secrets, private data, tokens, and unrelated user information.

steps.description: Fetch the authorized URL once and record status plus selected fingerprint headers and bounded derived body/cookie signatures.

Match target fingerprint, vendor/CPE hints, owner-confirmed version evidence, CVE, reviewed-template status, external search evidence, and authoritative advisory metadata against local and public candidate sources, then generate non-exploit evidence gates and a gated validation-attempt plan.
